author: HSinghHira
description:
Ente is a self-hosted, end-to-end encrypted platform to store, share, and rediscover your photos and videos across all your devices.
**Features**
- End-to-end encryption for every photo and video you upload.
- Web app for your library plus a separate public-albums app for
  sharing.

- PostgreSQL for application data and MinIO (S3-compatible) for object
  storage, both bundled and pre-wired.

- Bundled Mailpit catcher for sign-up verification codes — no SMTP
  setup required to get started, with the option to switch to a real
  provider later.

- Per-account storage cap automatically raised well beyond the
  10 GiB free-tier default (configurable or removable).

- Persistent storage under /DATA/AppData/$AppID for both Postgres and
  MinIO data.

**How to use?**
1. Open Ente Photos from the Zima OS dashboard.
2. Complete the initial setup and create your administrator account.
3. Sign up for an account in the web app.
4. Retrieve your verification code from the bundled Mailpit catcher at
   http://<IP>:8407 (or your real inbox if you've configured
   SMTP).

5. Start uploading photos and videos, and set up a public album to
   share with others.

6. SMTP delivery, the storage cap, and S3 endpoint hostnames can all be
   changed later via the service environment variables — no rebuild
   required, just a container restart.

tips.before_install:
1. **Server Endpoint:** http://<IP>:8403
2. **Mail Server:** http://<IP>:8407 (no login required unless
   you set MP_UI_AUTH)

2. This app ships with working sample passwords and keys so it
   starts instantly — change-me-* values on the museum, postgres,
   and minio services (ENTE_DB_PASSWORD / POSTGRES_PASSWORD,
   ENTE_S3_B2_EU_CEN_SECRET / MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD) plus
   ENTE_KEY_ENCRYPTION, ENTE_KEY_HASH, and ENTE_JWT_SECRET on
   museum — before storing real photos.

4. ENTE_DB_PASSWORD must match POSTGRES_PASSWORD exactly, and
   ENTE_S3_B2_EU_CEN_SECRET must match MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD exactly —
   update both sides of each pair together.

5. **Important:** changing ENTE_DB_PASSWORD or MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD
    later without also updating the already-initialized
    Postgres/MinIO credentials will lock museum out — a manual
    credential update inside that container (or a fresh volume) is
    required.
